newsitem.title: UK: Analysts see limited Clyde impact on UK E&P sector.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see limited Clyde impact on UK E&P sector.

text.p: Shares in Britain's oil exploration and production (E&P) sector will only receive a moderate boost after Gulf Canada Resources narrowly won control over Clyde Petroleum, analysts said.
They expect that a fair number of investors who sold or tendered their Clyde stocks will not re-invest all their money in other E&P shares following recent oil price weakness.

"I wouldn't say the sector is going to have a big leap up after this. There may be people who regard the E&P sector as being slightly overvalued at the moment," said one analyst who declined to be named.
"Some people are taking profits now anyway with the oil price coming back," he added.
Gulf Canada earlier announced it held 51.42 percent of Clyde Petroleum after its 494 million stg hostile bid closed at 1300 GMT.
One of Clyde's major shareholders, PDFM, has already announced it would not re-invest its money in the oil sector after the fund sold its 14.9 percent stake to Gulf Canada last week, analysts said.
But the lower oil price since the beginning of the year would not cool the takeover fever which has increasingly gripped the E&P sector worldwide in the past one and a half year, analysts said.
After years of cost-cutting and efficiency drives the oil industry is awash with cash and ready to make acquisitions to boost reserves.
Gulf Canada's bid may have failed to attract a counter offer -- many pundits had predicted one -- but that does not mean takeover interest in the E&P sector has diminished, analysts added.
"The fact there wasn't a counter bidder for Clyde does not rule out more takeover activity in the sector," said Colin Smith at broker BZW.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see one more (bid) before the year. People have the cash and the sector is much better managed. There are some incredible targets out there," said another analyst.

But shareholders and potential predators alike will have to look harder for cheap stocks after the E&P sector gained strongly last year following a succession of takeovers and positive news on oil finds.
"You have got to be lot more selective than last year because then the whole sector was going up. This year you have to look for the real value," said this industry watcher.

In an unperturbed E&P sector, recent star performer British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc was up 2-1/2 at 1,277-1/2 pence, while Monument Oil and Gas Plc -- a stock considered relatively cheap by some analysts -- firmed two pence to 85-1/2.
